note.question: What determines a canonical quantity-based network revenue management problem where a firm accepts or rejects incoming customer requests irrevocably in order to maximize expected revenue given limited resources?
note.overview: The model considers a canonical quantity-based network revenue management problem where a firm accepts or rejects incoming customer requests irrevocably in order to maximize expected revenue given limited resources. Because of the curse of dimensionality, the exact solution to this problem by dynamic programming is intractable when the number of resources is large. This paper studies a family of re-solving heuristics that periodically re-optimize an approximation to the original problem known as the deterministic linear program (DLP), where random customer arrivals are replaced by their expectations.
